newsitem.title: NIGER: Protest violence marks Niger poll anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Protest violence marks Niger poll anniversary.

text.p: Opposition activists clashed with security forces in Niger on Tuesday after defying a protest ban on the first anniversary of Ibrahim Bare Mainassara's transition from coup leader to elected president, witnesses said.
At least one person was hurt and four people arrested in the capital Niamey, where security forces deployed at key intersections and near opposition party headquarters, the witnesses added.
Police sources reported further arrests in the towns of Maradi and Zinder, hundreds of km east of the capital, when protesters set fire to tyres in the street and hurled stones at security forces.
Interior Minister Idi Ango Omar announced a ban on all demonstrations on July 7 and 8, saying the government had had reports that violent protests were being planned.

"We cannot, in conformity with the penal code, tolerate demonstrations aimed at continually disturbing public order and inciting citizens to rise up and take arms against the authority of the state and against one another," he said.

Mainassara, who toppled elected president Mahamane Ousmane in January 1996, scrapped the independent electoral commission on day-two of polling last July. Security forces took control of ballot boxes and the count took place in the absence of representatives of opposition political parties.
The opposition cried foul but the supreme court confirmed the result. The United States suspended aid in protest.
Mainassara took power after a stand-off between Mahamane and his prime minister paralysed government for over a year.
